text: Given credentials whose role has Gateway | Policies | Read, When mimecast_list_policies is called with type="blockedsenders", Then it returns a JSON list with count, has_more and next_page_token.
Given the same credentials, When mimecast_list_policies is called with type="antispoofing-bypass", Then it returns that type's policies in the same list shape.
Given a policy id returned by mimecast_list_policies, When mimecast_get_policy(type, id) is called, Then it returns that single policy's fields.
Given an id Mimecast does not recognize, When mimecast_get_policy(type, id) is called, Then it returns a not_found error envelope instead of raising or returning an empty 200.

Given a sender and a recipient mailbox address, When mimecast_manage_sender(action, sender, to) is called without confirm: true, Then no request reaches Mimecast (recorder.api() is empty) and the tool returns done: false with an explanatory message.

Given the same call repeated with confirm: true, When mimecast_manage_sender is invoked, Then it POSTs {action, sender, to} to /api/managedsender/permit-or-block-sender and returns done: true with the sender/recipient/type echoed back.

Given Mimecast rejects the permit-or-block-sender call (e.g. the role lacks Gateway | Managed Senders | Edit, returned as a fail[] item), When mimecast_manage_sender is called with confirm: true, Then the tool returns the standard structured error envelope, not a raw exception.

Given credentials whose role is missing the required permission (Gateway | Policies | Read or Gateway | Managed Senders | Edit, simulated as an HTTP 403 from Mimecast), When any of the three new tools is called, Then the error envelope's code is "unauthorized", matching the same generic classify_status mapping every existing tool already gets (no new code path).
notes: No dedicated 403 test is required beyond the existing generic classify_status coverage already exercised by test_api_client.py (see test_bad_client_credentials_are_unauthorized); the two cited tests exercise the same error-envelope path for the new tools' call sites specifically.

text: Given a request to /mcp missing the X-Mimecast-Client-ID / X-Mimecast-Client-Secret headers, When tools/call is attempted for any of the three new tools, Then the gateway middleware rejects it with 401 before any tool code runs and before any request reaches Mimecast.
notes: Covered by the existing generic, path-level middleware test (parametrized over missing/blank/placeholder header combinations) — it runs ahead of tool dispatch, so it already covers the three new tools with no test change required. Cited here, not duplicated, per docs/tickets/PRD-21236.md Non-functional section.

text: Given two concurrent requests with different Mimecast credentials, When each calls one of the new tools, Then neither request's credentials or response data leak into the other (per-request isolation, no shared state at module level).
notes: Covered by the existing generic concurrency-isolation test; not tool-specific, no test change required.
